_what: Uber Base, harvested from the Principal's OWN duplicate of the Base Gallery. The authoritative catalogue: 131 component sets, 3,425 variants, every set carrying its real variant axes and its component key.
_why_this_replaces_what_came_before: Everything this programme has said about Base until now rested on two weaker things. `Base (redrawn)` in the master Figma file is SIXTEEN sets I drew by hand in Base's idiom - an approximation of a 131-set library, and the Principal's words for it were "not right at all", which the numbers agree with. `uber-base-contracts.json` reached 72 of a believed 126 sets by walking Gallery instances one at a time. This is the whole library in one read.
_how: The Gallery copy holds ZERO components and 74 frames of instances - duplicating a remote library copies instances, not components, which this repository had already recorded. But an instance still NAMES its source: the REST response carries a `components` map of 3,516 entries and a `componentSets` map of 131, every one with its key. So the library is fully addressable through a file that contains none of it.
_access: GET /v1/files/4mz4UC3nacI6UFEXnyzFJc/nodes?ids=3:4200&depth=4 - 31.7MB, HTTP 200. The file is OWNED by this account, so the plan-tier budget that blocks third-party files does not apply.

what_it_corrects.base_redrawn_page: 16 sets, hand-drawn, against a real 131. It is a STYLE STUDY and must not be read as Base. The register cites it for 15 block types.
what_it_corrects.uber_base_contracts_json: reached 72 sets by walking instances; the denominator it used (126) was itself a guess. The real number is 131.
what_it_corrects.and_what_survives: base-axis-reconciliation.json is SOUND. All 14 of its rows record a Base axis set that exists VERBATIM in the real library - checked by comparing sorted axis-name sets. It saw a partial library and was accurate about the part it saw.

_what_this_is_not: A copy of Base into the master file. The components live in the Base LIBRARY file, which is not subscribed here; this reads their names, keys, axes and variant counts and draws nothing.
Enough to place a real Base instance. That needs the library enabled on the target file, which is a Principal action - `libraries_available_to_add` is empty.
A reading of what any of them LOOKS like. No fill, radius, type or spacing is read: this is the contract surface, not the pixels.
